title: Believe
coreMove: earn buy-in by understanding the mission deeply enough to explain its purpose without spin or borrowed language
sourcePressure: Resistance to the Iraqi partner-force mission changes when leaders understand and explain why building partner capability matters.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: make people believe by sounding confident

sourceAnchors.name: Iraqi partner-force mission
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says SEAL resistance shifts once leaders understand why building Iraqi capability matters strategically
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Iraqi partner-force mission should land as the moment where orders prove thinner than belief until the why becomes clear.

sourceAnchors.name: SEAL resistance to the Iraqi partner-force mission
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses the resistance to show that authority can create participation before it creates conviction
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The resistance is useful because it shows disciplined people can still carry a mission as rented work when the purpose has not reached them.

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: mobile vaccination team asked to serve a distrustful rural fairground
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic lead whose nurses think the assignment is political theater
exampleSpecs.stakes: families will skip care if the team arrives resentful and unable to explain the purpose
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead admits her own doubts, calls the county nurse for the real access problem, then explains the fairground plan in terms of missed appointments and transport gaps
exampleSpecs.firstImage: folding vaccine privacy screens lean against a cattle-show pen at dawn

exampleSpecs.domain: university archive staff moving rare documents for a flood-wall project
exampleSpecs.audience: an archive director facing staff anger about disruptive relocation
exampleSpecs.stakes: the move can damage trust and irreplaceable materials if people treat it as pointless
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director studies the flood-risk map, walks staff to the lowest stacks, and explains why the temporary move protects access instead of just ordering boxes packed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: blue flood-line sticker sits three inches above a row of acid-free boxes.

exampleSpecs.domain: software privacy migration that slows feature work
exampleSpecs.audience: an engineering manager with developers angry about deleting legacy data
exampleSpecs.stakes: rushed compliance work can turn into resentment and sloppy migration
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager stops selling the deadline, reads the user deletion request history, and explains the migration as keeping a promise users already made visible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: data-retention ticket shows a user request that has been waiting forty-three days.
mustAvoid: legal fear as the only why

exampleSpecs.domain: wildlife crossing build that closes a popular trailhead
exampleSpecs.audience: a park ranger whose crew is tired of visitor complaints
exampleSpecs.stakes: the crew may enforce the closure harshly if they do not believe in the purpose
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the ranger reviews the collision reports, walks the crew to the underpass survey stakes, and has each person practice explaining the closure in one honest sentence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Orange survey ribbon flutters beside fresh deer tracks near the highway fence.

exampleSpecs.domain: food bank changing pickup rules for partner pantries
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations lead whose volunteers think the new appointment system is needless hassle
exampleSpecs.stakes: families may receive less food if partner pantries keep arriving in clumps
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead shows volunteers the previous week’s spoiled produce count, connects it to uneven pickups, and has them test the new appointment sheet before explaining it to partners
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: crate of wilted cilantro sits beside a clipboard of late partner pickups.

exampleSpecs.domain: orchestra section asked to adopt an unpopular slower tempo
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal violinist leading musicians who think the conductor is overcorrecting
exampleSpecs.stakes: the section can comply mechanically and still make the passage lifeless
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the section lead listens to the singer’s breath mark, has the violins play both tempos, and asks which one lets the phrase land before defending the change
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: penciled breath mark circles one measure on the violin part?

skillTargets: test whether a leader actually understands the why
turn compliance problems into purpose explanations
reject spin, pressure, and borrowed language as false belief

tryThisNowSpec: Take a task people resist and explain the real why in two plain sentences without using authority, urgency, or because I said so.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
